posts.title: Book Review: Rising Thunder by Neal Shusterman
posts.description: Book: Rising Thunder by Neal Shusterman Genre: YA dystopian Rating:⭐⭐⭐⭐ Wow... if you are a fan of the Arc of the Scythe series, you will NEED to read this one! This the prequel... all the stuff that led up to the events in that series (and I think this one is going to be a full series too?) and answers a bunch of questions like: How did the AI (the Thunderhead) get formed? Who created it? And how did there end up being one AI fighting for good and one fighting for bad... at least that's what it looked like as a reader. THEY didn't think of it that way of course! How did all the people who started the Scythes get together? And who were they? Diamonds are explained...and cloaks. And scythes. Who were the first people saved with nanites...the things that can erase disease? How did that even get going and who invented it? And how did they decide immortality wouldn't work??? posts.title: Monthly Reading Wrap Up: October 2026
posts.description: Here's what I read this month: Lady Tremaine by Rachel Hochhauser: This one is in the running for my favorite book of the year. Loved SO MUCH this retelling of Cinderella from the step mom's POV. Such an interesting take on this story with an awesome back story and very interesting twists. So good!⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Falling Like Snow by Misty Wilson: This is a holiday/Christmas companion novel to Falling Like Leaves, which is a fall holiday story. This one follows a different couple and is very fun and cute and sweet, just like the first one. I love this series a lot! This one was an ARC read from Netgalley.⭐⭐⭐⭐ Theo of Golden by Allen Levi: Finally managed to get to this very buzzed about book. I thought it was nice and heart warming, but maybe not as PERFECT as everyone was cracking it up to be. Still, it was very enjoyable to read. The plot is simple, and old man comes to town and befriends everyone as he gives away the portraits found in the local coffee job.⭐⭐⭐⭐ Light Up My Life by Kasie West:

posts.title: Book Review: Beginning to Look A Lot Like Us by Sara B. Larson
posts.description: Book: Beginning to Look A Lot Like Us by Sara B. Larson Genre: Holiday romance Rating:⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ I loved this romance! One of those stories where when I was reading it, I was thinking about the characters and wanting to get back to them to find out how it's going down. This is the story of Clara, who finds out her boyfriend broke up with her during an interview on national TV. She's a popular author and was telling everyone about her book, when someone dropped this news. It also happened at the same time her grandmother died. Everything feels like it's falling apart. Later, at Christmastime, she goes to her grandma's house to take care of some things. She plans to fix up the house to sell it. While there, she finds out the the guy she hung out with for many summers when she'd come to visit her grandma, is back and living next door.
